analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES - Debate on datacentres implications; AMD & Arista beat; Scout beats; Auto1 trims guide; Wolters solid; Liberty targets CMA
key_insights: SOX rebounded 2.5% ahead of US midterm results but closed below its intraday high of +4.2%. US desk activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale, with semiconductor and AI flows more balanced as selective buying absorbed some of the ongoing selling. MU +2.6%, Hynix ADRs +2.1%, NVDA +2.3%.

AMD and Super Micro each gained about 7% after hours on better-than-expected revenue outlooks. Arista rose 10% after hours (the desk's post-bell line says +6%), with an outlook pointing to AI revenue doubling to $7bn. Semiconductors gained a further 2% after the close.

The desk is focused on what the Democratic sweep means for data centres and AI, particularly Texas, which accounts for about 27% of planned US data-centre capacity. The initial concern is whether the shift weighs on development. Some X commentary suggests the new policies may be less negative than feared because existing players are already meeting many of the Hinojosa asks.

The question after the recent semiconductor and AI sell-off is how much policy risk is already priced. Tuesday's rallies preceded the election results and are context, not proof of discounting: CIFR +18.4%, HUT +16%, WULF +14.5%, GLXY +15.4%, IREN +11%, NBIS +7%, CRWV +7%, BE +9%, GEV +6.5%, VST +3.7%.

The US TMT trader described a more balanced two-way market, with selective buying absorbing some semiconductor and AI selling. Recent sessions had little buying support. Meta and Oracle traded well after their recent capital raises, and the market's ability to absorb heavy AI issuance remains important.
GS sees some conditions investors wanted starting to fall into place, at least partially: earnings delivery, financing, some relief in oil and rates, and resets in positioning and valuations.

Credit strategy (Amanda Lynam) estimates $657bn of year-to-date global AI-related debt issuance across syndicated credit markets through November 2, and says the scale is much larger than the five hyperscalers alone.

Per an FT article cited by the desk, AI-related CDS net notional is about $30bn (ex-CRWV) versus under $7bn a year ago. The 10 main names are about 14% of US single-name CDS open interest and about 20% of volumes. Oracle is the largest and most active (weekly volume about $2.3bn, open interest about $7bn) and is the credit proxy for the AI build-out. NVDA 5Y CDS is about 141.5bp.
Per the FT, Oracle scrapped a chip leasing contract with Tencent worth an estimated $7bn.

AMD Q3 revenue was $13.38bn (+45% y/y) versus $13.11bn consensus. Data Center sales rose 97% to $8.55bn versus $8.25bn expected. Q4 revenue guidance is about $17bn (+66% y/y) versus $16.29bn consensus, with implied EPS of about $2.92 versus $2.65 consensus. Gross margin of 55.94% missed, Q4 margin guidance of about 55% is 30bps below consensus, and Client revenue fell 3.7% q/q. GIR reiterates Buy.

Arista: Q3 revenue, EPS and margin beat, 2026 revenue guidance raised to imply 48% growth, and an initial 2027 outlook of 38-40% revenue growth, 62-64% gross margin and about 49% EBIT margin. AI revenue is guided to double to $7bn and campus to reach $2bn. GIR raises 2027/28 EPS by about 10% to $6.13/$7.83. Declining deferred revenue and slowing bookings growth are the key concerns.

Super Micro F1Q27: EPS $1.81, revenue $19.9bn, gross margin 12.8%. FY27 revenue guidance raised to $72-82bn from $65-72bn. Cash conversion cycle improved by 52 days q/q to 97 days with $3.1bn of customer prepayments. One customer was 44% of revenue, and competition from ODMs and OEMs could keep margins volatile.

Shopify fell 9% on a mixed print: GMV missed, growth decelerated for a second straight quarter (34.8% in Q1, 31.6% in Q2), and revenue was only in line after at least 12 straight beats. The Q4 gross profit guide (high-twenties growth) missed the roughly 30-31% expected.

Dynatrace fell 16.6%. It beat on subscription revenue, margins and EPS, but the FY27 ARR guide raise reflects only the Arize acquisition and EPS guides missed (FY $1.88-1.90 vs $1.96 Street, F3Q $0.44-0.45 vs $0.50) on Arize dilution and about 11M more shares.

Scout24 beat Q3 on revenue and adjusted EBITDA by about 1% and raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to about 18% from 16-18%. German professional subscription revenue was 2% below expectations. GS notes the Street is already there.

Auto1 results were in line with the pre-close release, but the company says it is supply constrained and now expects units and gross profit mid-range and adjusted EBITDA at the lower end of FY26 guidance. The stock is expected to be under pressure.
Wolters Kluwer 9M26 organic growth was 6% versus GSe 5%, a rounding beat with all divisions in line. Full-year guidance was reiterated.

Liberty Global's call was aimed at the CMA, challenging its approach to Netomnia. A CMA final report is expected in mid-December. Liberty will not build a third UK fibre network and is considering all asset-sale options to deleverage. VMO2 leverage is well into the 6x range versus a 4-5x target. The Ziggo Group spin is reiterated for Q2.
10Y yield backed up to 4.96% after JOLTS of 7.523M versus 7.164M estimate, and rate-sensitive pockets underperformed.
Post-bell moves: PCOR +13% on revenue acceleration to +19% y/y and cRPO +29% y/y. BKNG fell 7% after guiding to a sharp y/y deceleration in Q4 room nights.
Reports of worsening HBM shortages in China under US export restrictions, and DeepSeek reportedly plans to train its V5 model mainly on Huawei Ascend 950 chips in 2027.
